newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end unchanged in heavy trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end unchanged in heavy trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed virtually unchanged on Monday despite heavy trading by provident funds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.01 pct to 100.68
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 pct to 100.42.
Volume was a high 224 million shekels, with trading in Makams reaching 100 million shekels.
Traders said the strong volume was due to heavy trading by the big provident funds. "Redemptions from the funds have almost stopped and they have more money to invest," said one trader.
"CPI-linked bonds closed unchanged despite slightly higher demand. The market is very stable and we can see that there are no sellers," said Roy Meir of Simodan.
"Unlinked bonds were also stable as investors wait to see if the Bank of Israel cuts interest rate following the release of December's CPI," Meir said.
The December inflation figure is due to be published on December 15, and the Bank of Israel will announce February interest rates on January 27.
"The Makams rose slightly but this is only part of a steady rise, which is nothing unusual," the other trader said.
Traders said dollar-linked bonds rose following the decline of the shekel against the dollar. On Monday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2470 shekels against 3.2420 on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
